descriptions.pc88:local-0db2f5521e: A simulation: as a member of the earthquake prediction committee, read geological data to forecast when the big one will strike and keep the economic damage down.
descriptions.pc88:local-0e22a78160: A visual novel in which a girl whose mother is bedridden sets out on a journey to find a cure for her illness.
descriptions.pc88:local-0e4b94d561: The first 100 Yen Disk compilation: Shooting Master '86, an adventure that leads into a fixed-screen shooter; Graman Bee, a space shooter about blasting space worms for power-ups; an electronic novel; the Breakout imitation The Rotten Wall; and the one-life spike-jumping runner Jumpper.
descriptions.pc88:local-0e6a890032: An Onion Software compilation disk mixing doujin games with CG, preview screens and game programming engines.
descriptions.pc88:local-0e82ab1668: A CG collection disk of digital illustrations by HAGA-KEN, one of the best-known PC-88 doujin CG artists.
descriptions.pc88:local-0f5d551e66: Active Gamers' third 100-yen disk magazine (1993), built around their RPG Undine with a corner covering the game, an Undine music mode and a collection of previously unreleased PC-88 music.
descriptions.pc88:local-112861eb52: A quiz game: told by the king that he may wed the princess only by answering questions, the hero defeats the court officials one by one in quizzes; its current-events questions were already years old on release.
descriptions.pc88:local-11749f90fc: An unofficial fan port of Namco's Bosconian: fly through space destroying enemy battle stations by knocking out their outer cannons or hitting the core, while dodging fighters, missiles, meteors and mines and catching the escaping spy ship.
descriptions.pc88:local-119a248df5: A 2D wireframe battle game that won LOGiN's software contest and was sold through Brother's Takeru machines: in 989 New A.D. the giant creature Gavither returns with a huge meteor, and a newly found fighter must stop him for good.
descriptions.pc88:local-11b5f6ebab: A quiz game by the SIVA collective with help from Burning Apple, Creative H.A.T., G.Create and SSG, where each girl has her own artist and quiz category, and music by Onion.
descriptions.pc88:local-11b609b080: One of five Firecracker music disks released together in 1990 for 200 yen each, covering video game music programmed in BASIC MML under ALPHA-mini DOS, which traded some sound quality for a large track count.
descriptions.pc88:local-122aa09a3b: Firecracker's first-anniversary issue (1991), its fifteenth disk in a single year, adding livelier PCM loading screens, a handier track selector and staff credits that roll over the ending theme of Dragon Slayer: The Legend of Heroes.
descriptions.pc88:local-1240ead271: A blackjack-like card game in which reaching 21 is not always best and going over is not always a loss, with three tries against each opponent.
descriptions.pc88:local-1311ce2393: Burning Apple's sequel adventure with action elements, in which the hero leaves his body as a spirit; its artwork was later carried almost unchanged into the commercial Sweet Angel from Active.
descriptions.pc88:local-132a8f29e1: A doujin sequel to Bothtec's The Scheme, made quickly by the same staff and sold only once at Comiket: a brutally hard action game pairing Ys III-style side-scrolling with The Scheme's shooting, with a surreal streak of flying cows and Sound Board II music by Yuzo Koshiro.
descriptions.pc88:local-13a589ab10: A Ryokusui Sound Team music disk featuring a large selection of Dragon Quest III arrangements.
descriptions.pc88:local-14004dcb7f: A dungeon-crawling RPG: buy weapons, armor and a spell, then search a dungeon for pompoms, choosing to fight, cast or flee in random encounters.
descriptions.pc88:local-14823964ad: The quietly released third episode of Amazing Disk, OSS's TRON Computer Diagnosis, which tells a story the player advances by answering yes or no.
descriptions.pc88:local-149673c68b: A comic adventure that is really a minigame collection: otaku Arashi Tanaka travels to the end of the Edo period, where Ryoma Sakamoto kidnaps his time-machine-inventing relative, and must win minigames to recruit great figures from history, starting in ancient Egypt.
descriptions.pc88:local-1511cfcadc: A Firecracker music disk made for Comiket 42 in August 1992, composed, arranged and programmed by CHEMOOL with PMD: doujin originals and arrangements from Tetraforce, Vapor Trail, Atomic Robo-Kid, Midnight Resistance, Dirt Fox and X68000 Bosconian, among others.
descriptions.pc88:local-15c6f60e07: A doujin horizontal shooter built as a near one-to-one copy of Irem's R-Type.
descriptions.pc88:local-163243cb20: ASCII's shogi game, with eight levels up to amateur first dan, tsume-shogi problems of up to fifteen moves, and printed game records.
descriptions.pc88:local-164b4123dd: Elein Soft's first software release (1987), after three earlier volumes appeared in print: as manga artist Miki Kawada, go out picking up girls in search of material for your work.
descriptions.pc88:local-1671cffd8e: Firecracker's 1990 music disk devoted to Konami SCC-chip tunes such as Gradius II and Parodius, with a PCM-voiced Chichibinta Rika theme as its centerpiece.
descriptions.pc88:local-17219482a8: Probably the first doujin disk magazine, by BERO of Dennou Kagaku Kenkyuujo, promoter of the Pi image format: his columns plus playable trials of the circle's games, handed out at Pasoket events for the price of the disk.
descriptions.pc88:local-182d3714f8: Team TBL's Tetris clone with a normal mode, where clearing a set number of lines advances the level, and an endless mode played until all lives are lost, both speeding up as they go, plus a music mode.
descriptions.pc88:local-185de07406: LOGiN magazine's first original tool, introduced in its November 1986 issue: a PC-8801 kit for building your own Ultima-style overhead RPGs, often cited as a forerunner of RPG Tsukuru.
descriptions.pc88:local-187ec06f9c: An adventure about Kimiko Suzuki, a first-year schoolgirl at St. Francisco Girls' School, who runs into her junior-high classmate Sakaguchi in a park.
descriptions.pc88:local-19cdf8546b: A top-down adventure in the style of Old Village Story: a young woman searches the Forest of No Return for her lover, who went exploring there, avoiding beasts and monsters with her wits rather than fighting.
descriptions.pc88:local-1b30983a09: An adventure in which the hero finds a purse and must return it to the right person; wrong choices leave him empty-handed.
descriptions.pc88:local-1b78077d6b: A 1991 Firecracker disk heavy on Dragon Saber and Dragon Spirit music, also featuring Actraiser with string PCM samples, picks from E.D.F. and Kengou, and original pieces by guest composers.
descriptions.pc88:local-1c07557f83: A card game played with mahjong-tile symbols: the player and the computer take turns placing cards, and each placement changes a map on the board.
descriptions.pc88:local-1cc03f0f93: A placement puzzle in the spirit of the eight queens problem: put the randomly offered pieces where they match no piece in the same row or column by color or pattern until the quota is filled, with a help function and swappable data disks of other designs.
descriptions.pc88:local-1cf6fbf91e: A 1985 adventure whose original story and script were written by science-fiction novelist Sakyo Komatsu; commands are chosen with the function keys and the player moves with the numeric keypad.
descriptions.pc88:local-1d1e69c4a3: The first Imagical Musion Depot (1994), a 35-track anthology that Active Gamers produced for the Takeru vending machines with well-known doujin musicians including NT-3, Monden, OSATOH, yon and Anima.
descriptions.pc88:local-1d66f03498: Released in 1993 after a year-long gap, this Firecracker disk covers four titles: Sword Dancer, the X68000's Little Chinese Final, Gravity Response and Variable Geo.
descriptions.pc88:local-1de468366b: A doujin RPG about a young man on an island who fights monsters and human enemies while buying better weapons and armor.
descriptions.pc88:local-1e8c1567ae: A collection of solitaire games played with cards, mahjong tiles and colored panels.
descriptions.pc88:local-207a81fdfe: A naval simulation: command the sailing ship Thousantis in semi-turn-based battles against other ships, and perhaps find land to go ashore.
descriptions.pc88:local-20b0d31cfe: A three-disk RPG set in a Wizardry-style wireframe dungeon where the enemies are girls, in the manner of Chaos Angels, with puzzles and events along the way and art by ASUKA.
descriptions.pc88:local-213e3f94ee: A 1990 Firecracker disk of minor game music, covering rarely arranged titles such as Cyber Tank and Atomic Robo-Kid; it loads PCM much faster than earlier issues and hides a 31st track that only plays when the computer's clock is set to December.
descriptions.pc88:local-216cf4302d: A three-disk RPG also sold on Takeru: Areos, son of a hero, travels a demon-ridden land after the sword that once sealed an ancient god, in an episodic multi-scenario story with adventure-style towns, a map for travel, and first-person battles that raise stats after every fight.
descriptions.pc88:local-223582517d: A Plotting-style puzzle game: throw the block in hand to remove matching blocks against a time limit, aiming to finish with only three blocks left.
descriptions.pc88:local-228f7fe835: A card game whose title mimics Xevious: the economic control system Yyeleiss has run amok, and the player must beat its three guard computers at Nine Card, which turns out to be the Japanese game Kabu; the girl beside the table plays no part.
descriptions.pc88:local-23909abe74: A fixed-screen shooter in which a spellcaster blasts slimes and other creatures; each very different boss defeated adds a new spell to the starting fireball.
descriptions.pc88:local-2433618eee: A dating game: choose one of four women and win her over in conversation.
descriptions.pc88:local-25a9edf319: A tile-matching puzzle in the manner of Shanghai: turn over all 136 mahjong tiles in matching pairs.
descriptions.pc88:local-26df82d72b: A vertical shooter made with the shooting-game editor included in Tatesuka Wars.
descriptions.pc88:local-2710c7fb8f: A demo built on the first ending song of the anime NG Knight Ramune & 40.
descriptions.pc88:local-275956cba7: Junichi Ueda's second music disk: arrangements from Turbo OutRun, Galaxy Force, Burning Force, The Legend of Valkyrie, Power Drift and Night Striker, a few of Ueda's own compositions, and odd covers such as the children's song Oyoge! Taiyaki-kun.
descriptions.pc88:local-28a9118bcf: Zeal Soft's 50-yen command-driven romance adventure: a schoolgirl who fell for Hiroshi after he hit her with a football as a child tries to win his heart years later.
descriptions.pc88:local-29389b0036: Released alongside volume 33 in 1996, this Firecracker disk is built around the Harlem Blade soundtrack with further tracks hidden behind a keyboard trick, and was apparently the circle's last new music disk.
descriptions.pc88:local-2a870cb1c7: Extra scenarios for Sorcerian produced by Conrad T. Ozawa and supervised by Falcom: five adventures, among them The Two-Headed Hellhound.
descriptions.pc88:local-2ace156d08: A vertical shooter made with Tatesuka Wars' editor: choose which power-up to take from those dropped by enemies, clear the screen with wipers, and face bosses; a PC-98 sequel followed.
descriptions.pc88:local-2b756e52be: A 1992 edition of NT-3's music disk Yume no Fantasia for computers without a Sound Board II: the same content on the standard FM sound, minus the game music corner, for 41 tracks.
descriptions.pc88:local-2be6088c6c: An Arkanoid-style block breaker whose ball only rebounds at 45-degree angles.
descriptions.pc88:local-2c5fff9afa: A board game in the manner of Monopoly: buy up tourist spots and grow rich on the dice, with place names and chance cards you can rename and computer players who react as they play.
descriptions.pc88:local-2de00a3014: An election simulation: run against six other candidates through a 24-day campaign of posters, speeches and bribery, which can get you arrested, before voting day on June 30.
descriptions.pc88:local-2e77372cee: A war simulation themed on the Gulf War, opening with a debt-ridden man picking a fight with a wealthy girl; the weak Kuwaiti army makes pushing back the Iraqi forces very hard.
descriptions.pc88:local-2f406a13a0: Shogi with Kōji Tanigawa: play five opponents with their own favorite strategies, solve forty tsume-shogi problems, or pick the best next move.
descriptions.pc88:local-2f918727c2: A doujin adventure about a band of schoolboys.
descriptions.pc88:local-2fae9ca69f: The second Sadistic Gamers quiz from Sixteens (1990): a student struggling with his studies takes a supplementary lesson from his teacher, and answering her questions well moves the lesson along.
descriptions.pc88:local-2ffc37d2b7: Megafeps' third collection of original compositions (1992), bright tunes with high bell-like melodies and darker pieces driven by restless bass lines and syncopation, plus a guest track by Firecracker's CHEMOOL.
descriptions.pc88:local-312f8c6ffb: A parody of the classic Star Trek strategy game, also released on the FM-7.
descriptions.pc88:local-318afc3e84: A board game for one to four players that claims to be about life but is really about spreading your color across the board, entirely at the mercy of the die.
descriptions.pc88:local-32569dc182: ECE Software Factory, pioneers of doujin quiz games, made this 1987 quiz with graphics by NAO Graphics Lab and title music by a young Yuzo Koshiro.
descriptions.pc88:local-325b05751c: An adventure on a mysterious island populated mostly by young women: talk to people, examine things and wander around to learn what the island is about.
descriptions.pc88:local-32aae853c8: A 1991 Firecracker collection of hard-edged covers from Bosconian, Actraiser, Genocide, Lagoon and The Scheme, plus a standout Night Arms arrangement, alongside one contributor's renditions of Wink and Yuki Saito pop songs.
descriptions.pc88:local-32b6fa36c7: A block-pushing puzzle in which the player, a heart, moves blocks to steer a young woman who walks on her own toward the exit door.
descriptions.pc88:local-32c2ca5469: Onion Software's 1986 parody RPG in the Ultima mold: rescue a princess held deep in a dungeon, with gags throughout, cameos by other doujin circles, punishing difficulty and a hidden Majaventure picture as a bonus; it was one of the magazine-featured titles that first made doujin software known.
descriptions.pc88:local-333938f279: A side-scrolling action game in which a knight rescues fairies over adventures of four levels each, with bosses guarding keys, food to restore health, and items like a magic wand, flying shoes and a harmful skull.
descriptions.pc88:local-345c11bee4: Three-way rock-paper-scissors with your partner Yukari against a third girl.
descriptions.pc88:local-34eb44de6a: NT-3's first music disk for Active Gamers (1990): 53 tracks, mostly NT-3's own compositions, for the standard FM sound only, with a bonus corner reached by pressing Return on the title screen.
descriptions.pc88:local-357ed50ec1: A fantasy adventure in which Kain, arrived from another world, travels with Myutika, whose black hair marks her as cursed in this land, to defeat the demon king.
descriptions.pc88:local-35a7e8ae4e: Onion Software's last PC-88 release (1990), the seventh 100 Yen Disk: the all-weather shooting action game The Busy Home Town, TSUKKA Software's Space Hanazukin-chan and Creative H.A.T.'s racer Yoshio-kun Dasu P!! Mawarunda, with music from eight composers making full use of PCM.
descriptions.pc88:local-37a59c5a74: G_Club Software's 1989 action game: rotate and thrust an inertia-bound craft called the Hunter to reach the goal within the time limit, with cute girl graphics and music by KAJA.
descriptions.pc88:local-382fc5f0bc: Swimming-loving schoolgirl Mia plans to stop at a crepe shop with her friend Eriko after school; art by Fozon.
descriptions.pc88:local-38ae9b0226: A Tetris clone where clearing the required rows lets the player choose between the next level and a harder one.
descriptions.pc88:local-38c80bbbe1: A battle-focused, Wizardry-style 3D dungeon RPG where defeated monsters can join the party; it was distributed copy-free with an on-disk manual.
descriptions.pc88:local-39d5a08552: A very short Alice in Wonderland adventure in which Alice follows the white rabbit down the hole and the player only picks between two choices at each step.
descriptions.pc88:local-3a6344405b: An FC-Software disk of minigames including Rich Racer (collect dollar signs), a bungee jump scored on depth, a number-mashing cartwheel race and a money grab that speeds up each level.
descriptions.pc88:local-3a8265f6ec: ALU Computer Arts' 100-yen bundle of a mostly original music collection and Phrenetic Shooting, a fast fixed-screen bullet-dodging shooter that stood out when most doujin games were slow picture-story adventures.
descriptions.pc88:local-3c26a5bbdd: A dice-driven board game with RPG and strategy elements: from the starting inn, stop the rolling die, then fight, hire soldiers or even get drunk depending on the space, aiming to reach and slay the dragon.
descriptions.pc88:local-3c74c3abf3: Firecracker's eleventh music collection (1990), given over almost entirely to Gofer no Yabou Episode II tunes, with CG by Akira Araki; it began using the Sound Board II's 256 KB of RAM as a RAM disk, a buggy feature that led to a second version without it.
descriptions.pc88:local-3c9409437e: A two-player-only action game set in a future where war has been replaced by arena battles between tanks that can jump.
descriptions.pc88:local-3f88451dc9: Third game in Scatter Brain's shooter series after Crinex, this time a vertically scrolling shooter with forgiving difficulty; an illustration follows each cleared stage, and a no-continue clear on Hard is said to change the ending.
descriptions.pc88:local-3fa6691416: Selected Sorcerian 2: two prize-winning scenarios from the Sorcerian scenario contest, Pandora's Box, in which the evils let out of a box must be put back, and The Scorching Trap.
descriptions.pc88:local-402b77dd9f: A puzzle game: drop playing cards into a five-by-five grid to make poker hands across its rows, columns and diagonals.
descriptions.pc88:local-4030ace524: Selected Sorcerian 1, the first of the Sorcerian scenario contest winners: The Beautiful Bride and The Town Where the Silver Light Went Out, with a magazine disk.
descriptions.pc88:local-4068e9e83e: A novelty disk from Black FTZ: a yellow wire-frame Nadia figure dances all over the screen to an endlessly looping PCM recording of the 'Yashi no Mi Natera' dish-soap jingle. It was ported to the PC-88 after a warm reception on machines like the PC-98.
descriptions.pc88:local-41ab0f09fc: Falcom's utility disk for Sorcerian: easily create any of 120 spells, rename items and characters, move characters between save disks, and shop at a store with limited stock that displays whatever you sell, plus extras such as a board game, a quiz and a music mode.
descriptions.pc88:local-446e51b88a: First of the three self-booting Amazing Disk episodes, introduced by a 'mysterious Amazing Disk' narration; this one holds Onion Software's game Box Express Flying in the Sky.
descriptions.pc88:local-458d267711: Fifth disk in Onion Software's 100 Yen Disk series, made with outside circles: Creative H.A.T.'s Fuusen, OSS's sushi puzzle and Jumper 3, the series' first Sound Board II game, with music by Yuzo Koshiro and Shinji Hosoe.
descriptions.pc88:local-47159519a0: Third disk in zeal soft's Splash series, nominally an adventure game though the author admits it barely works as one; it features mostly male characters, music by Waki, and a deliberately slack bonus quiz mode.
descriptions.pc88:local-47c885c13b: Tsukumo's yakyuuken rock-paper-scissors game, a hit among the many versions of the time, by Tadashi Makimura (Mari-chan Kiki Ippatsu) and based on one he drew in his Shonen Magazine manga Micom Love.
descriptions.pc88:local-4c63068657: School-themed side story starring the girls of Fairie's Residence, subtitled Sailor-fuku to Hitobanjuu; like the other Specials it came with a comic that ties in with the software.
descriptions.pc88:local-4c9ce39c6f: Three quirky PMD music disks by zeal soft's Kamijo: vol. 1 has a free-talk corner recommending ramen shops over PCM horse-race commentary, vol. 2 a real-time scaling title screen, and vol. 3 oddly named tracks and a menu that appraises your PC-88's resale value.
descriptions.pc88:local-4e4e6a8a25: Second 100 Yen Disk omnibus sold at Comiket: Wincrolizeth (dive into a vortex past a boss lifted from Fantasy Zone), the image-guessing quiz Karleloa and four-player block breaker Rotten Wall Jr., the Darius-themed volleyball game Darai Ball, Jumpper II and the first Sushi Game.
descriptions.pc88:local-4e8f41f6a9: Orphe's fourth PC-88 music disk, first sold at Comiket 44 and made for the Sound Board II; it carries fewer tracks than earlier disks but adds a bonus game.
descriptions.pc88:local-4f1a953694: Third issue of Champion Soft's disk magazine Omega, containing programs such as Uketsukejou ni Attack and Osaka-jou Adventure.
descriptions.pc88:local-4f3a603287: A numbers-driven baseball simulation for one or two players: call the pitch's course, type and speed, and give detailed orders at bat and on the mound.
descriptions.pc88:local-4fdf493dca: A 3D wireframe flight simulator: fly the Red Wing with ailerons, rudder and elevator, take off and land, and destroy enemy fighters, factories and the super colony's control computer.
descriptions.pc88:local-4ffe05ffd3: LOGiN magazine's follow-up to Adventure Tsukuuru, the first 'Tsukuuru' maker, published in the October 1987 issue: a tool for building command-selection adventure games that adds support for pictures.
descriptions.pc88:local-500c90deec: A horizontally scrolling shooter programmed by ZURA, the release that launched Charlie Soft as a doujin circle.
descriptions.pc88:local-511844f9fd: Princess Mefilia of planet Pure, destroyed by planet Gear, joins the army of planet Utia to take revenge and uncovers one conspiracy after another in this three-part science-fiction adventure on six disks; wrong commands mean instant death.
descriptions.pc88:local-5142735591: A fantasy adventure with unusual automapping, built as a campaign system: later scenario disks such as Oono-san Panic and Ninja Keisatsu run on the same engine.
descriptions.pc88:local-5142a09799: A two-disk PMD music collection from Exiz, mainly new pieces from an RPG and from Dragon Star, including Denshou, which drops voice samples into its rhythm over a driving bass line.
descriptions.pc88:local-5180cd9c16: A hero convinced he is a gambling genius sets out to conquer the world, loses at poker to a girl in a bar, and learns a huge gambling syndicate stands behind her. Color poker duels use life gauges and usable items.
descriptions.pc88:local-525450aeb8: Firecracker's ninth music disk, a small feature on Akumajou Densetsu and Ys music, with a Dirt Fox track crammed into about 13 KB, Kuuga (later bundled with PMD as a sample) and an original by Hacker magazine contributor Yoshinori Mori.
descriptions.pc88:local-529fbd912e: Second in Lolita Soft's gentle fairy-tale adventure series about Sayoko, with a story of girlish sentiment like the first; the single-color graphics come from its move to 400-line mode.
descriptions.pc88:local-5328d40756: Firecracker's seventh music disk, the first to switch to the PMD driver and to use PCM samples, and the first to add illustrations, establishing the screen layout the series kept from then on.
descriptions.pc88:local-53d423428c: Third in SSL and Peach Land's card game series, an RPG-flavored game with only four card types: cards are turned up by luck, attack cards reveal more of the picture according to their strength, and monsters cost hit points.
descriptions.pc88:local-5441baff28: The first sample disk for FSD, Frostforest's very compact FM music driver for the PC-88, running on their large FROST-DOS, with tracks by MKR, Monden, yon", Osamu Ishikawa, Active Gamers' NT-3 and SHYNER.
descriptions.pc88:local-5487435e63: A two-disk picture gallery: a skeletal host welcomes the visitor to his 'mansion of demon girls' far from the human world, after which around sixteen pictures of its girls by manga artist Senno Knife are shown; there is essentially no game.
descriptions.pc88:local-563034addc: A 1991 digest collection of Fairytale's games sold only through the TAKERU software vending machines, including a digest version of Lipstick Adventure 2.
descriptions.pc88:local-577bd9d604: Junichi Ueda's second music collection from PSG Soft, with arrangements from Turbo OutRun, Burning Force, Valkyrie no Densetsu and Night Striker, several Ueda originals and odd covers such as Oyoge! Taiyaki-kun; the '+' edition gives the originals titles.
descriptions.pc88:local-579183d0c6: A best-of disk from the music circle Orphe that packs the disk with its original and game music, centered on Hasegawa's compositions and opened by a striking logo effect; it was sold at Comiket 43 to 46 in slightly revised editions.
descriptions.pc88:local-58e0335cc1: A poker variant played with seven kinds of illustrated cards, seven of each, so hands get their own names such as 'Only You' and 'Sister'; points earned change the large on-screen picture of the opponent.
descriptions.pc88:local-58f4c3a2ea: A fill-in-the-blank adventure in the style of HARD's Kindo Gals: hidden words in the text must be replaced by a word of the right length to win the girl over. This volume features 15-year-old schoolgirl Asuka Kato, a gym committee member who is bad at sports.
descriptions.pc88:local-596fcae3ba: The final chapter of Tsukka Software's Spirit series of field-map RPGs, an unusually large doujin release on eight disks with music by CHOBIN; only the opening demo uses ADPCM, and a hidden alternate opening is included.
descriptions.pc88:local-598faad68e: A science-fiction adventure: a crew sent to survey ruins left by aliens runs into a mysterious radar image, a swarm of asteroids and a girl caught up in a dimensional rift, with mini-games along the way.
descriptions.pc88:local-59ad2c7d71: A parody of DB-Soft's Konya mo Asa made Powerful Mahjong played as rock-paper-scissors against three girls, with one or two hidden opponents.
descriptions.pc88:local-59f5a88433: First of four side stories starring the girls of Fairie's Residence, subtitled Mariko no Ikenai Daitokkun; it came with a comic that ties in with the software.
descriptions.pc88:local-5af36afec6: A detective adventure: a school detective club looks into the case of a runaway student.
descriptions.pc88:local-5bf590e48b: Third Phrenetic Shooting from ALU Computer Arts, a dodging-focused shooter with even denser enemy fire than before and bosses for the first time; every enemy shot down is worth just one point.
descriptions.pc88:local-5c4ceeccc2: Firecracker's 19th music disk, highlighted by Mishima's Sound Board II arrangement of Revolter, a small Yuzo Koshiro feature and originals by Ishikawa and Monden, plus Junko Ozawa's Standard Theme; the cover art is by Kenichi Minoda.
descriptions.pc88:local-5c545f7179: Selected Sorcerian 4: The Goddess Who Vanished into Darkness, the contest's only scenario by a woman, and the Chinese-flavored Youmugen Legend with jiangshi and pandas.
descriptions.pc88:local-5de0852c85: A computer version of jankyuu, the mahjong-themed pinball-style parlor game, offering three machines and two-player play; developed by Coconuts 21 for Victor's CrossMedia Soft label.
descriptions.pc88:local-5ef27a06bd: A score-attack shooter from Firecracker: score as much as possible within two minutes. Results differ by machine speed and Sound Board II presence, and a replay mode feeds the per-model rankings printed in Firecracker's music disks.
descriptions.pc88:local-5fe26392e7: Firecracker's 22nd music disk and its second CHEMOOL originals special, dressed in Kazuhiko Shimamoto-style hot-blooded art and built around music for the mahjong game Tekken Seisai, Nouten Chokugeki! 3 and CG collections from KDD and D-TEN.
descriptions.pc88:local-606b58458f: A word game: as Kazuki Kuremoto, win girls over with words alone by picking the right replies; wrong answers make you drink milk until the game ends.
descriptions.pc88:local-6098c418fa: An adventure combined with a stage-clearing puzzle game on four disks; booting from the PCM disk with a Sound Board II makes the birds and the girl speak, and a puzzle construction mode is included.
descriptions.pc88:local-61f5bf743e: An animated crossword game with eight bunny girls and fiendishly hard puzzles.
descriptions.pc88:local-62d2be5fcf: An RPG starring an ordinary slime who answers the king's call for heroes after Princess Imu of Slime Land is kidnapped by an evil sorcerer; the game bills itself as made for a mental age of 12 and under.
descriptions.pc88:local-64ac59e131: A doujin adventure: the lively student Morina is having a busy day as usual when she finds herself in a mysterious world.
descriptions.pc88:local-650148c957: Specters' take on Mastermind: deduce the hidden code by trial guesses, which a little logic cracks in a handful of tries, making it a quick break between longer games.
descriptions.pc88:local-652a230891: A collection of four-panel comics starring Miki from Champion Soft's disk magazine Zeta, with parts of some panels animated.
descriptions.pc88:local-669628406a: A side story to Yuugekitai: a submarine suddenly appears off the coast, and the squad returns to uncover its secrets.
descriptions.pc88:local-66fcce00b7: ASCII's construction kit for horizontally scrolling shooters (the name puns on 'yoko scroll'): draw the player ship, enemies and backgrounds, pick the music and set enemy movement patterns to build your own game. Sold through TAKERU vending machines around 1988.
descriptions.pc88:local-6762fa6299: Tsukka Software's first release, a two-disk field-map RPG from 1987 that began the Spirit series, continued in Umi no Mukou (Spirit 2) and concluded with the eight-disk Dragon Knights.
descriptions.pc88:local-682c16a63d: Firecracker's 16th music disk, given over to CHEMOOL's own compositions, including music written for doujin releases such as Tetra Force and Hanayaide Osaka, plus a hidden patch fixing a track from the previous issue.
descriptions.pc88:local-682f623b30: As a new teacher at a girls' school, you are infatuated with student Kumiko and must fend off the other schoolgirls while trying to arrange private after-school lessons with her.
descriptions.pc88:local-692c1ca51d: First issue of Champion Soft's 'graphic idol magazine' Zeta, a disk sold with a printed magazine that created fictional idols and presented their profiles and pin-up pictures, along with some games.
descriptions.pc88:local-69f28649e9: A blackjack game against a fiercely strong computer, ported from Iron Gear's X68000 and MSX2 versions by Firecracker's AQUA under the Mad Pierrot name, with Sound Board II music and pictures that scroll across two full screens.
descriptions.pc88:local-6a9348e87e: Show-business side story starring the girls of Fairie's Residence, subtitled Super Mariko Sisters and played as a sugoroku-style board game; it came with a tie-in comic.
descriptions.pc88:local-6af4b781a2: A war simulation of the Battle of the Coral Sea: lead up to four fleets toward Port Moresby against the American fleet in semi-real time, never knowing the enemy's losses until the end.
descriptions.pc88:local-6b731819f9: A panel-sliding puzzle like a pipe game: a bunny shifts whole rows or columns of 24 wrap-around panels to link the start and goal panels within a limited number of moves.
descriptions.pc88:local-6d82d2cd53: A 100-yen pack of four bizarre games from Ayashige Soft, including two 'Miyamo' games, a moxibustion game using the members' own relatives as material, and a fashion contest.
descriptions.pc88:local-6dcb106ed4: A Bomberman-style action puzzle for one or two players: set off the bombs scattered around the field in chain reactions to drain the opponent's endurance to zero. Simple rules hide a lot of strategy, and the explosion animation is elaborate.
descriptions.pc88:local-6df7f2739c: A parody of Little Red Riding Hood: sent by her mother to visit her grandmother, she faces traps all along the way.
descriptions.pc88:local-6f39223cd3: A comic show-business adventure on three disks: newly hired at TKO Production, you are ordered to scout new idol Yonami Watanabe and make her a top star. The title screen uses a photo of Minayo Watanabe.
descriptions.pc88:local-6f801134ae: Third music disk from Yanbaru Kuina, with illustrations by Fox and a very fast custom DOS by K-na that adds striking visual effects to the tracks.
descriptions.pc88:local-6f9b24f378: Music software for the PC-8801's Sound Board II, supervised by Koichi Sugiyama, with sample arrangements included.
descriptions.pc88:local-70df9f50d9: A science-fiction adventure set in 2552: find the weakness of the alien Danak to save the colony planet Farras.
descriptions.pc88:local-71069a4604: Second of the three self-booting Amazing Disk episodes, holding OSS's game Jinsei no Katachi (The Shape of Life).
descriptions.pc88:local-72b5843706: A song-themed adventure from Active Gamers (August 1991) played with RPG-style top-down movement in the manner of The Old Village Story; the NT-3 music disk Mysterious Love Token 98 came with it as a bonus.
descriptions.pc88:local-740abcad30: The fourth FSD sample music disk from Frostforest, celebrating Chaikuro joining the circle with his originals across many genres, including pieces written for the X68000 RPG Kaze no Tabibito and a hardcore techno track built on orchestra hits.
descriptions.pc88:local-74a234ab16: Sixth volume of Marionet's Take Out fill-in-the-blank adventures, in which a boy visits a café whose waitresses wear sailor uniforms.
descriptions.pc88:local-75543c5958: Charlie Soft's first music disk, played through the PC/M88 driver with its distinctive SSG sound: mostly original tunes plus rarely heard picks such as the battle music from Sangokushi and the opening of Jesus.
descriptions.pc88:local-7656e5ebb2: A doujin adventure: a girl gives the hero a key, and that night a mysterious dream begins.
descriptions.pc88:local-76beaf6729: Chosen to play the fugitive in a WASP special police training drill, you must escape a 3D maze generated anew each time, armed only with a stun gun and a Star Blade while nine teammates hunt you; stats come from an Ultima IV-style personality quiz.
descriptions.pc88:local-787477e14c: A Team Dangeroude music disk running on FROST-DOS with the FSD driver, including Puyo Puyo music and another essay by Yamazaki.
descriptions.pc88:local-79375663c5: A chess game with four levels, saved games, and a problem mode of mate-in-three puzzles.
descriptions.pc88:local-7a3b474127: A doujin adventure: win the heroine Milady, with many encounters along the way.
descriptions.pc88:local-7a9eddf314: First game in Kankyouken's Aya-chan series, known for its distinctive cute art: an adventure with a rather harsh scenario told at a leisurely pace.
descriptions.pc88:local-7c9212e048: Kurosawa's world-scale strategy game for Camadamia Soft (1990), built around pointed profiles of the world's dangerous leaders, written before the Gulf War yet seeming to foresee it; it is the only game to use zeal soft Kamijo's sound driver.
descriptions.pc88:local-7cfec59cec: A singing disk on which Karasawa plays guitar and belts out Tsuyoshi Nagabuchi's Doshaburi Rainy Day, played back as PCM synthesized through the PSG.
descriptions.pc88:local-7d2a360d88: A free disk Active Gamers handed out in August 1992 to mark two years since forming, recording the circle's history and even including a glossary of its in-jokes and terms.
descriptions.pc88:local-7ee53fbbca: Part IV of Oak's Fantastic Cubic line, a three-dimensional color-matching puzzle developed by Kyoto Computer Brains and released in 1983.
descriptions.pc88:local-804fe7c10a: TSUKKA software's event disk for Comic Market 41, named after NEC's Bazaar de Gozaru mascot: a board-game quiz and a racing game with text-based scaling and rotation, full PCM voices and a music room for Chobin's tunes.
descriptions.pc88:local-80aa019898: Active Gamers' second 100-yen extra disk (1992), packed with a rejected scenario from their game Infinitia, a music collection and a complete walkthrough of Holiness Story.
descriptions.pc88:local-80baa19ac4: First volume of Pasoket's own Kagai Jugyou series, an idol-themed multiple-choice quiz with pictures of pretty girls, made by Nihon Art Media for the label of the doujin software fair organizer and released on four disks in 1989.
descriptions.pc88:local-81109b62c9: Sequel to Burivary System's futuristic blackjack game Medal Jack, needing the first disk to play; the rules stay the same while the girls are new.
descriptions.pc88:local-81842b4b52: One of Firecracker's first five music disks, released together at 200 yen each and written in BASIC MML for Sound Board II.
descriptions.pc88:local-8359f7ed21: A 20-stage puzzle game like Flappy: guide a witch pushing blocks until the light-blue block reaches the goal, using items that flip gravity and magnets that pull blocks.
descriptions.pc88:local-837968b3a6: A card game packed with parodies that runs on a fake operating system called Humen8.8K: win money at poker and blackjack, then gather items for an RPG-style battle against a boss.
descriptions.pc88:local-83d0a93346: A war game of World War II in Europe, North Africa and Arabia from the invasion of Poland to 1945: one to five players command six great powers' land, sea and air forces in three-month turns.
descriptions.pc88:local-840e8708b9: A doujin music disk compiled by Macha, playing tracks from Nihon Falcom's action RPGs Ys and Ys II on the PC-88's FM sound.
descriptions.pc88:local-84a8d9d450: NT-3's 1992 music disk for Active Gamers, the first of their collections to officially support both Sound Board II and the standard FM sound.
descriptions.pc88:local-84ec0ef9d2: Five games, a jigsaw, a matching panel, a quiz, a crossword and a horoscope, each hosted by a girl aged 12 to 21.
descriptions.pc88:local-86380815e7: Looks like an RPG but is really a field-map adventure, full of absurd twists such as a station attendant turning out to be a CIA spy.
descriptions.pc88:local-86b16101fd: Second volume of Pasoket's Kagai Jugyou multiple-choice quiz series, themed on high-school girls, made by Nihon Art Media and sold under the label of the doujin software fair organizer in 1989.
descriptions.pc88:local-87116f933e: Selected Sorcerian 5: Go! Doto's Triathlon, a parody race with huge prizes and no danger of death, and The Seal, the hunt for an escaped werewolf convict on a remote island.
descriptions.pc88:local-875ea13e5f: Part of Kanai Karasawa's Kimochi Disk 2: the same looping photographed dance idea in a Japanese style, flanked by Nio guardian statues, with sampled sound produced through the beeper.
descriptions.pc88:local-8787c3adae: Elein Soft's follow-up short adventure, Kanami-chan no Nichiyoubi: Kanami Saeki spends her Sunday, with Yumika returning and newcomer Mariko among the friends she can invite. Each run takes about ten minutes and branches toward different pictures.
descriptions.pc88:local-88266f5afc: This time the training is bomb disposal: in a maze that changes every game you have 40 minutes to find and defuse a bomb, which may be solid or liquid and must have its wires cut in the right order.
descriptions.pc88:local-88b339b5b5: Frostforest's FSD music sampler billed as Chaikuro's best background music, filled almost entirely with original tracks by Chaikuro and Monden.
descriptions.pc88:local-8a4cfcddd6: Baseball played as a board game: take your team around the camp, season and other sheets on the dice against five computer teams.
descriptions.pc88:local-8bc545ef6f: An action game in which you steer a small craft through zero-gravity mazes against the clock, fighting the craft's inertia to make it go where you want; Bardy Soft later reworked it with new graphics as its commercial debut, Hole Chaser.
descriptions.pc88:local-8be727dcdf: PC-88 port of Yasunori Takahara's MSX type-in from LOGiN's conversion corner (November 1986). In this real-time adventure you have slipped past the guards into the mansion and must find the hidden secret documents before time runs out, juggling a limited set of carried items.
descriptions.pc88:local-8c9f60642f: A late (2006) Firecracker music disk built around Fishcafe's Onii-chan to Issho and many original tracks from guest musicians.
descriptions.pc88:local-8ce9cb4b55: A puzzle game starring a foul-mouthed evil rabbit who has to steer a girl lost in the forest into his house by placing fences.
descriptions.pc88:local-8d1389fca7: Mink Label's four-disk table game crossing Old Maid with mahjong; the graphics are attractive, and completing a winning hand is notoriously hard.
descriptions.pc88:local-8d379d1bed: A fiendish picture puzzle: swap tiles to complete several images at once, but each tile has two faces and flips every time it moves, and later stages split the pictures into more pieces.
descriptions.pc88:local-8e45f5b649: A blackjack card game from G.Create, makers of the FLAT music driver, starring a pair of blue-haired sisters animated in full colour, with Sound Board II music.
descriptions.pc88:local-8e6d06118a: Orphe's best-of disk, packed with original and game music for the PC-88 (Sound Board II recommended); this Comic Market 45 edition differs from the earlier C43 one only in its comments and version.
descriptions.pc88:local-8f3c416a8f: A 33-track NT-3 music disk from Active Gamers (1991), the first of the circle's releases with full Sound Board II ADPCM support.
descriptions.pc88:local-8f8ebcaa81: A chaotic adventure from Camadamia Soft: the girl every classmate admires has been kidnapped and the police are getting nowhere, so with school out you set off to rescue her yourself.
descriptions.pc88:local-8fdf969fac: The high-school-girl volume of Marionet's Take Out series: Rui brings her friend Noriko to the school infirmary to join her and Kiyomi, and as before you progress by typing the words hidden behind blanked-out text. With three heroines it grew to two disks.
descriptions.pc88:local-8fe969f580: A simulation game from Creative H.A.T. in which you pilot mecha and wipe out the enemy, sold with a thick manga by FoZon explaining the side story.
descriptions.pc88:local-907236b647: The king will marry his daughter to whoever climbs his castle first: roll 1-5 to climb, but a 6 drops you to the start unless you have hammered in a stake, which takes a roll of 4 or more. Timing the stakes against your rival is the whole game.
descriptions.pc88:local-918000a033: A short Elein Soft fantasy adventure: rescue Princess Eris from the witch Sadiral, helped by Amil, a timid girl who swears to obey you. A run takes about ten minutes, and replays are needed to see every picture.
descriptions.pc88:local-927110fe0d: One of Firecracker's first five music disks, released together at 200 yen each and programmed in BASIC MML, which kept the sound modest but the track counts high.
descriptions.pc88:local-92cfa45448: A dice-driven board RPG from Dennou Kagaku Kenkyuujo, the circle behind the Dennou Tsuushin disk magazine: dice move your hero around the board and also settle every battle, much like Compile's Rune Master.
descriptions.pc88:local-9373354336: Part of Kanai Karasawa's multi-disk Kimochi Disk 2: pick Kanai or Karasawa and play look-this-way against him; win and he strikes a photographed come-hither pose with a recorded voice.
descriptions.pc88:local-940934fc51: Firecracker music disk devoted to Tenshindo, mainly Martial Age and Yan Yan no Quiz Icchomae.
descriptions.pc88:local-9421da146b: ALU Computer Arts' signature shooter: blistering speed and enemies that fill the screen with bullets, while your ship is nearly powerless and survives on a life gauge, so the game is all about dodging.
descriptions.pc88:local-94d4c34605: Go and gomoku on a nine-by-nine board, with a lesson mode that teaches the rules of Go.
descriptions.pc88:local-95a99dd08f: Magazine-style personality quizzes from eight girls.
descriptions.pc88:local-95f9e4a5ed: A fantasy adventure, often called the first doujin software: the hero searches a fairy-tale world for a bride, talking to people and animals and solving their problems.
descriptions.pc88:local-969cc3afcf: A short Elein Soft adventure, Kanami-chan no Doyoubi: you guide the girl Kanami through her Saturday by simple choices, optionally calling over friends Michiyo, Yumika and Misano. A play takes about ten minutes, so repeat runs reveal the rest of the pictures; a bonus compatibility quiz unlocks extra art.
descriptions.pc88:local-9755c596c3: TKO Soft's Donjara tile game with its own scoring hands: when hero Susumu's childhood friend is carried off by a gang of tile players, he infiltrates their hideout and takes on its members, whose tiles and hands follow their hobbies, such as pro wrestling or progressive rock.
descriptions.pc88:local-97781249ab: Second Tabibito no Gakufu story from Team AB: while Rune is staying with a girl named Shurea, he clashes with the local count, again carried by its music.
descriptions.pc88:local-97bea4d8a3: A grim RPG: after his house burns, his father is murdered and his mother dies of grief, young Selen wanders off to make a living, fights monsters and uncovers the demon lord's plan. Battles are elaborate in a tabletop-RPG way and progress is saved with passwords.
descriptions.pc88:local-983fa780be: A word quiz of odd trick questions whose answers appear with some letters blanked out; each correct answer unlocks the next picture.
descriptions.pc88:local-985005f82a: A two-disk blackjack game from Cream Soft: on Christmas a girl dressed as Santa drops by and promises a present if you can beat her friends, among them schoolgirl Kaori in her sailor uniform, Chisato, Nagisa and Sayo. The computer gets a little stronger with each opponent.
descriptions.pc88:local-98722ec031: A parody of DB-Soft's Konya mo Asa made Powerful Maajan that swaps the mahjong for rock-paper-scissors against three girls, with a hidden character or two.
descriptions.pc88:local-98b015e019: Frostforest's FSD music sampler with a small Romancing SaGa feature, followed by originals from GEPPEL, Osamu Ishikawa, NT-3, yon", Monden, KEN and Chaikuro.
descriptions.pc88:local-98fbf37d5b: A one-on-one fighting action game against parodies of familiar anime characters, each attacking in a style that suits them and getting a knowing gag when beaten.
descriptions.pc88:local-997b30ec89: Tien Gow, the Chinese domino game, in which you bet on which of four hands is strongest, for one player against three set opponents or for four people.
descriptions.pc88:local-9982e5f66c: Active Gamers' four-disk 1993 RPG, a tale of devotion between siblings that was two years in the making and aimed at being the strongest doujin RPG on the PC-88. Its 34-track score was written in Sound Board II, standard FM and PSG versions, and it was among the last PC-88 titles still sold on TAKERU.
descriptions.pc88:local-9a1c726225: First of Team AB's Tabibito no Gakufu series, a digital picture story in which Rune, dressed like Snufkin, is caught up in a small trouble in a village on his travels, with music placed front and centre.
descriptions.pc88:local-9a52d415b9: Third issue of Champion Soft's Zeta idol disk magazine, sold with a printed booklet and starring its regular cast of teen idol girls: a top-ten news corner, a date between a reader and idol Minaho, a jigsaw puzzle and more.
descriptions.pc88:local-9a574eef3f: A quiz made for the 1990 Osaka Flower Expo in which every question is Expo trivia; the prize for winning turns out to be not the girl on the title screen but the bizarre talking creature Hanazukin. Its Sound Board II music by CHEMOOL is unique to the PC-88 version.
descriptions.pc88:local-9c57481492: A Sengoku strategy game: five great warlords, among them Takeda Shingen and Uesugi Kenshin, compete through march, battle and intrigue phases taken in a random order each turn.
descriptions.pc88:local-9d61a798ff: KOB soft's reverse Othello: the winner is whoever ends with the fewest pieces. Three opponents scattered across Japan's cities make up ten stages with different starting layouts, and the music supports Sound Board II.
descriptions.pc88:local-9d6f5f4a3b: LOGiN Soft's construction kit for field-map action RPGs, an ancestor of RPG Tsukuru sold through TAKERU in 1988: draw graphics dot by dot, lay out map chips and build your own game. Named after explorer Mamiya Rinzo; a sample game is included.
descriptions.pc88:local-9d8d2f9afe: A text adventure by Thinking Rabbit: four hundred years ago Queen Madeleine died in prison for trying to poison her father, yet her portrait shows no trace of evil; set out to learn the truth.
descriptions.pc88:local-9d983ff467: A free bonus disk for answering the survey in Active Gamers' Infinitia, carrying NT-3's music from the enhanced PC-98 edition of Mysterious Love Token back over to the PC-88.
descriptions.pc88:local-9de742bbd9: The sixth of ONION software's 100-yen disks (1989), with four games by ONION, OSS, G-Create and Creative H.A.T., led by Cattle Mutilation, a mysterious game about aliens, cows and UFOs; another stars Hikkoshi-kun, a character known only from Shizuoka TV ads.
descriptions.pc88:local-9e9585d0a7: Firecracker's tenth music disk, centred on Super Star Soldier and the first to drop the standard FM version for lack of space; it also slips in a tune from Hanayaide Osaka.
descriptions.pc88:local-9f6a762d8a: A DTB software magical-girl adventure: young Yuki visits an amusement park with friends and her fairy pet Pome, who vanishes; turning into Milky Pal and back, she searches the Ferris wheel, teacups and roller coaster and catches the pair who stole Pome.
descriptions.pc88:local-a028df090c: The only music disk made by all of Orphe's members together, for Sound Board II: it has many tracks and full-colour scanned pictures, which pushed it onto two disks.
descriptions.pc88:local-a2b3541c41: The 1990 finale of Elein Soft's fantasy series, told as a novel-style adventure: three years after rescuing and marrying Princess Eris, the hero has become king, until a woman from the kingdom's past steps out of a mirror and a witch turns out to be lurking inside his queen.
descriptions.pc88:local-a520827243: Firecracker's long-promised Dracula special: 51 tracks from the three Famicom Castlevania games and the Game Boy one, with plenty of documents.
descriptions.pc88:local-a627ba6355: A music disk by Kashinohinoki and Unoafuku of Team AB, playing refined original tunes through their own driver, which squeezes extra voices and drum sounds out of the standard FM chip.
descriptions.pc88:local-a6c0ce96fb: A backgammon-like board strategy game from Creative H.A.T. whose field map changes every stage, so tactics must adapt.
descriptions.pc88:local-a81fe7f0d7: A sample game for LOGiN Soft's early action-game editor, a forerunner of the Tsukuru series: your hero walks, crouches, jumps, swings a sword and hurls fireballs at enemies.
descriptions.pc88:local-a87527dd0b: A sliding 15-puzzle whose pictures and music, including a music mode, change when you insert a data disk.
descriptions.pc88:local-a8dde75b55: A command-selection adventure from Unique's: guide Miyou, locked in Gyokukakuji temple as a test of courage, to find her way out.
descriptions.pc88:local-a8ee758088: A concentration game in which panels carry a picture on both sides and pairs must be matched face-down; fewer panels can move each stage, and a challenge mode allows two-player matches.
descriptions.pc88:local-a905d2db16: Firecracker's third collection of guests' original music, including CHEMOOL's varied tracks for Nouten Densetsu and Osamu Ishikawa's Until the very end.
descriptions.pc88:local-aa578a3318: A tough falling-block puzzle from Frostforest in which you clear blocks by combining musical notes and rests, with a drill mode of set problems in the vein of Nazo Puyo.
descriptions.pc88:local-aac16c7308: A 1990 music disk from Kobe's Woodsman Club, running on Magical-DOS with the PMD sound driver.
descriptions.pc88:local-ab65d78e0a: An ASCII action game later collected on the Disk ASCII SF game disk: steer Rocketman with careful bursts of thrust to move between floors and collect every flower on screen, avoiding enemies and transformers and never hitting the ceiling or falling too far.
descriptions.pc88:local-ab6a347216: Starcraft's Japanese release of Sierra's Hi-Res Adventure #4, based on Homer's Odyssey: you sail to a magic land across the sea to bring back the golden fleece, getting past obstacles that only knowledge of Greek myth will solve.
descriptions.pc88:local-ab8cd403ef: Part of Kanai Karasawa's Kimochi Disk 2: ADPCM is loaded into memory, then frame-by-frame photographed dance animation streams from disk in an endless loop to MC Hammer.
descriptions.pc88:local-ac28261313: Firecracker's T-Square special music disk, arranging tracks from the fusion band.
descriptions.pc88:local-ac83ef8dd4: A 1988 Lolita Soft adventure produced by Ikuko Ebata, drawn in 400-line high resolution and accepting romaji command input.
descriptions.pc88:local-aca5cce1e3: Second Joker RPG, made entirely by one person: almost all text on screen, but with a carefully worked-out Dragon Quest-style scenario and music by Matsukui.
descriptions.pc88:local-ae8f1a8f3d: Firecracker music disk (1995) covering V.G. II, a piece made online on UNISON-BBS, and originals from the CD Alpha.
descriptions.pc88:local-aeffccb8e5: A late PC-88 RPG from A-Inn, a circle better known for its racier titles: a familiar quest to rescue the hero's kidnapped younger sister, released on two disks in 1991.
descriptions.pc88:local-afb48f2d0d: Firecracker music disk (1994) featuring Giga's Steam Hearts and Advanced V.G. plus the PC Engine Farland Story.
descriptions.pc88:local-b055fb23be: Team Dangeroude's second Hidoi Disk (1994), whose highlight is the mini game Yuukai Daisakusen, alongside more of Yamazaki's runaway essays.
descriptions.pc88:local-b15e4dceb8: A Seven Bridge card game whose underwear drawings were famously modelled on the Cecile mail-order catalogue, hence the title.
descriptions.pc88:local-b171141a21: A 2009 Firecracker music disk of quiz-game tunes: Capcom's Quiz Nanairo Dreams, Sega's Answer x Answer and Tenshindo's Yan Yan no Quiz Icchomae.
descriptions.pc88:local-b2372bc2aa: Bishoujo Club's card battle game: each card has a power and a number of actions, and you beat an enemy when your die roll plus power tops theirs; buy weapons for specific characters at the shop between stages, and save strong cards with few actions as trumps.
descriptions.pc88:local-b262361eba: The second parody fighting game, pitting you against stand-ins for Noriko, DAICON, A-ko, Kiki and Totoro on suitably familiar backdrops.
descriptions.pc88:local-b2ccdde7d4: A gallery of Adult Inn's 1987-1988 games, Ikenie no Machi and Bunny-chan no Himitsu among them, with a music mode.
descriptions.pc88:local-b3482fbcf4: Second issue of Omega, the older-skewing sibling of Champion Soft's Zeta disk magazines: guess which of four girls is the real model, follow college student Naoko through her day, and try an office-romance simulation.
descriptions.pc88:local-b40024ad29: ONION software's 1986 stage-by-stage action parody: to reach Rimi-chan, the girl who has just moved in next door, you face a run of trials that mash up Bouken Roman, Relics and other games.
descriptions.pc88:local-b407085538: A political simulation from DSK in which you play Japan's prime minister pursuing the annexation of Korea named in the title, battling public opinion while managing the political situation.
descriptions.pc88:local-b43811c2df: Part of Kanai Karasawa's Kimochi Disk 2: Kanai sings Shizuka Kudo's MUGO-n Iroppoi into a microphone, reproduced as PCM synthesized on the PSG.
descriptions.pc88:local-b4687b594f: A follow-up picture disk to Champion Soft's adventure Keiko-chan no Himitsu that imagines what became of its heroine Keiko, released in nurse, office-worker and new-bride parts of about five pictures each. The disk asks for a five-digit password before it runs.
descriptions.pc88:local-b4ad3ac440: TKO Soft's poker game, played under its own unusual house rules; the manual promises that anyone can reach the ending.
descriptions.pc88:local-b4ade00e5b: Fourth issue of Champion Soft's Zeta disk-and-magazine set: the booklet carries the four-panel comic Ganbare Maiko-chan and a profile of idol Miki, while the disk holds a spot-the-difference game, a jigsaw puzzle and a date with Kyoko.
descriptions.pc88:local-b4cc2b6e70: A 15-puzzle of pictures such as Iczer-1 with the key directions reversed, which makes it confusing to solve.
descriptions.pc88:local-b4fee200b1: A sliding puzzle: a digitized video clip breaks into pieces, which you put back together; third in the Peep Show series.
descriptions.pc88:local-b5894668a2: Mad Pierrot's PC-88 conversion of an entry in Iron Gear's Nouten Chokugeki series of card games.
descriptions.pc88:local-b96a0cf277: A doujin vertical shooter in which your ship has several firing options; you blast through waves of enemies to a boss in each stage, and clearing a stage earns a reward picture.
descriptions.pc88:local-ba5552b1d5: Firecracker's second-anniversary music collection: two pieces from Mother including Bein' Friends, a large helping of Streets of Rage and other Sega music, many tracks from Cotton and assorted Konami tunes.
descriptions.pc88:local-bb0aab6d8f: A role-playing game in the style of Wizardry: the space pirate ship Weird sets out again when it learns that an evil power granting eternal life sleeps on the planet Maria, with a party of five.
descriptions.pc88:local-bb3c7f5a75: A Go study program supervised by professional Koichi Kobayashi (then Judan), built to coach players working their way up to a 1-dan rank.
descriptions.pc88:local-bcff82c26a: The sequel to Irohanihoheto: the time-traveling warrior goes to Kyoto in 1582 to repair the history his last trip broke, so that the Edo shogunate lasts its three hundred years after all.
descriptions.pc88:local-be02986380: A time-travel comedy adventure: a student sneaks into school at night to fix a wrong test answer, is sent back to 1169 on the eve of the Genpei War, and must change history to fit his answer.
